tips.title: Selecting the Right Paint Type for Acrylic vs Enamel
tips.text: Acrylic paints like Vallejo Model Color (Item 12055) dry quickly and are ideal for base coats, while enamel paints such as Tamiya Enamel (Item 74001) offer a harder finish and better adhesion to glossy surfaces. For airbrushing, use Tami, AK Interactive, or AMMO by Mig Jimenez enamels for even coverage. Avoid mixing acrylic and enamel without a primer. Test on a scrap panel first to prevent marring. For weathering, apply washes with Alclad II (Item 36015) before enamels for enhanced texture.

tips.title: Choosing the Correct Sandpaper Grits for Each Stage
tips.text: Start with 400-grit sandpaper (P400, Tamiya) for initial shaping, then move to 1000-grit (P1000, Tamiya) for smoothing. For final sanding, use 2000-grit (P2000, Tamiya) to avoid scratches. Always sand in a well-ventilated area. Use a sanding block for even pressure. For delicate parts, use a fine sanding sponge (Tamiya) with 1000-grit for precision.

tips.title: Which Filler to Use for Gaps in Plastic Models
tips.text: Tamiya Plastic Putty (Item 82136) is best for filling gaps in plastic, providing a smooth finish. Vallejo Plastic Putty (Item 45112) works well for fine gaps but may shrink. For large gaps, use super glue mixed with baking soda (Tamiya Cement + 2% baking soda) for a quick, durable fix. Apply with a toothpick, let dry, and sand with 1000-grit sanding block. Always test on a scrap piece first to ensure compatibility.

tips.title: Selecting Photo-Etch vs Resin Detail Parts
tips.text: Photo-etch (PE) parts like those from Eduard or ICM offer intricate details but require careful handling with a brass brush and water. Resin parts from Clear Prop Models or Arma Hobby are stiffer and easier to bend but may need filing with a plastic file. For PE, use a 10% solution of Tamiya Cement (Item 87003) to bond to plastic. For resin, use a fine sanding stick and a 1000-grit sanding block to shape. Always test fit before gluing.

tips.title: Choosing the Right Decal Setting Solution
tips.text: Use Micro Set/Sol (Item 56803) for acrylic decal setting, applying 3-4 drops per decal. For enamel, use Mr. Mark Softer (Item 14144) with a 1:1 ratio of solution to water. Apply with a fine brush, let dry, then gently lift the decal with a razor blade. For best results, apply a gloss coat (Vallejo 7011) before setting decals to prevent wrinkling. Avoid using water alone as it can cause bubbling.
